title: Open API invoice lists never include the internal invoice
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Use an Open API key for the test organization, the Open API documentation, and a tool that sends API requests.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A, flagged as an Internal customer.
  • Have a new internal work order for this test, work order 1, for internal customer A, closed.
  • Have a new work order for this test, work order 2, for customer A, invoiced, billable, made before customer A was flagged, so a listed invoice can be compared.
custom_steps:
1. Send GET /v1/invoices.
  2. Send GET /v1/work-orders/[id]/invoices with work order 1's id.
  3. Send GET /v1/customers/[id]/invoices with customer A's id.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The response is 200.
  • Work order 2's invoice is listed; work order 1's internal invoice is not.

Step 2:

  • The response is 200 and lists no invoice.

Step 3:

  • The response is 200; it lists work order 2's invoice and not work order 1's.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11760 (Story 3, Close an internal or no-charge work order), story SV-11833 (Story 11, Open API and webhooks)

  • S3-R4: “No payment is recorded (not even the $0 payment a $0 invoice writes today) and no "Invoice paid" log entry is written, no customer transaction or receivable is created, no customer portal notification, email or invoice webhook is sent (the work order status webhook of Story 11 is), no invoice is sent to QuickBooks, the internal invoice is never listed in the Open API invoice lists and invoice.created and invoice.paid are never sent for it (both from the core release on, before Story 11), no tax, fee or discount is added, the shop supplies amount is not charged to the customer (it posts as an expense, Story 10), and the customer portal does not list the document (the portal vehicle list still counts a closed internal or no-charge work order for Last Service and Completed, as a service on the unit with $0.00 owed). Close and Reopen are recorded in the work order log as invoice created and reversed are today.”
  • S11-R2: “A closed internal or no-charge work order returns the status closed, a new value next to the existing ones, with its classification. Its internal invoice is never listed by GET /v1/invoices, GET /v1/work-orders/{id}/invoices or GET /v1/customers/{id}/invoices, from the core release on (S3-R4), so a consumer never has to skip it, and GET /v1/invoices/{id} answers 404 for it; the work order resource carries what an integration needs. Until this story ships, the work order reads invoiced in the API. Reopen returns the work order to completed.”
  • Terminology: “Internal invoice → the record created by Close. It is a third invoice state, Closed, neither Invoiced nor Paid, with no customer transaction and no payment. It carries the work order number (as every invoice does today; no number is consumed or skipped), has nothing owed, and is never sent to the customer, the customer portal or an invoice webhook, nor listed in the Open API invoice lists; QuickBooks gets no invoice; AccountingHub receives it as a Closed record with no revenue (S8-R1). Its date is the posting date.”
